I didn't have benchmark data to query, so these are priors from general NAS-Bench-201 behaviour, not measured results. Three heuristics drove most of the numbers.

- **Disconnected edits:** an edit on an edge that a "none" parent has cut off gains almost nothing, so the effect is lower under that condition (claim 6).
- **Replaced operation:** an edit replacing a weak operation (none) gains more than one replacing a conv or skip connection. Claim 27 is therefore higher, while claims 5, 7, 12, 14 and 18 are lower.
- **Removing an edge:** removing an edge that is already a weak pooling edge costs less than removing a conv edge, so claim 25 is higher.

Most other claims involve weak interactions between edges, so I kept them near 30–40.
